'''Juliet Michelle Daniel''' (September 19, 1964 – April 28, 2026) was a Barbadian-Canadian biology professor at [[McMaster University]], where her research focused on cancer biology. Daniel is recognized in the cancer biology field for the discovery and naming of the [[gene]] [[ZBTB33|Kaiso]], and was the recipient of several prestigious awards in recognition of her research and leadership, including an Ontario Premier Research Excellence Award and a Vice-Chancellor Award from the [[University of the West Indies]].

== Education and career ==
Daniel was born in Barbados on September 19, 1964.<ref name="globe" /> In 1987, Daniel completed a bachelor's degree in life sciences at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]], and then a PhD in microbiology at the [[University of British Columbia]] in 1993.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.blackincanada.com/2010/12/21/juliet-daniel/|title=Dr. Juliet Daniel|work=Black In Canada|access-date=2018-10-04|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_UtdQ6NsvYkC&q=%22Juliet+Daniel%22+Canada&pg=PA111|title=Who's who in Black Canada 2: Black Success and Black Excellence in Canada : a Contemporary Directory|last=Williams|first=Dawn P.|date=2006|publisher=Who's Who in Black Canada|isbn=9780973138429|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ronfanfair.com/home/2019/2/6/6ez4u94nxgsx65pu5wiffbmcrul2nq|title=Cancer researcher lauded for her leadership|website=Ron Fanfair|date=6 February 2019 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-07}}</ref> Daniel completed post-doctoral research fellowships for three years at [[St. Jude Children's Research Hospital|St. Jude Children's Research Hospital]], and then followed her supervisor's move to [[Vanderbilt University]], in [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]], [[Tennessee]], where she stayed for another three years.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://harryjeromeawards.com/portfolio-posts/dr-juliet-m-daniel/|title=Dr. Juliet M. Daniel - Harry Jerome Awards|website=harryjeromeawards.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-10-04|archive-date=2019-02-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190212011500/https://harryjeromeawards.com/portfolio-posts/dr-juliet-m-daniel/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During her fellowship, Daniel discovered the gene [[Kaiso (gene)|Kaiso]], and named it after [[Calypso music|calypso]] (a popular form of Caribbean music).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Daniel|first1=Juliet M.|last2=Reynolds|first2=Albert B.|date=1999-05-01|title=The Catenin p120 ctn Interacts with Kaiso, a Novel BTB/POZ Domain Zinc Finger Transcription Factor|journal=Molecular and Cellular Biology|language=en|volume=19|issue=5|pages=3614–3623|doi=10.1128/MCB.19.5.3614|issn=0270-7306|pmid=10207085|pmc=84161}}</ref> Daniel found that Kaiso transcriptionally regulates genes involved in [[cell proliferation]] and [[cell adhesion]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":5" />

Following her post-doctoral fellowship, Daniel joined McMaster University's Department of Biology in November 1999, where she was a full professor.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.biology.mcmaster.ca/faculty/|title=Faculty - Department of Biology|work=Department of Biology|access-date=2018-10-04|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801100006/http://www.biology.mcmaster.ca/faculty/|archive-date=2018-08-01|url-status=dead}}</ref> Prof. Daniel's lab studies [[triple-negative breast cancer]] (TNBC), specifically to identify genetic risk factors which may explain the prevalence and high mortality associated with TNBC in women of African ancestry.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thespec.com/opinion-story/8882220-dr-juliet-daniel-inspiration-personified/|title=Opinion {{!}} Dr. Juliet Daniel — inspiration personified|last=Mahoney|first=Jeff|date=2018-09-06|work=TheSpec.com|access-date=2018-10-04|language=en-CA|archive-date=2019-01-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190125092739/https://www.thespec.com/opinion-story/8882220-dr-juliet-daniel-inspiration-personified/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nationnews.com/nationnews/news/96286/bajan-nears-cure-breast-cancer|title=Bajan nears cure for breast cancer|work=www.nationnews.com|first=Tony |last=Best |date=April 30, 2017 |access-date=2018-10-04|archive-date=2019-03-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044343/http://www.nationnews.com/nationnews/news/96286/bajan-nears-cure-breast-cancer|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://brighterworld.mcmaster.ca/articles/cancer-biologist-juliet-daniel-honoured-with-harry-jerome-award/|title=Cancer biologist Juliet Daniel honoured with Harry Jerome Award|website=brighterworld.mcmaster.ca|language=en-US|date=April 24, 2017 |access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref> In 2017, Prof. Daniel's lab demonstrated that Kaiso plays a role in the proliferation and survival of TNBC cells.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bassey-Archibong|first1=Blessing I|last2=Rayner|first2=Lyndsay G A|last3=Hercules|first3=Shawn M|last4=Aarts|first4=Craig W|last5=Dvorkin-Gheva|first5=Anna|last6=Bramson|first6=Jonathan L|last7=Hassell|first7=John A|last8=Daniel|first8=Juliet M|date=March 2017|title=Kaiso depletion attenuates the growth and survival of triple negative breast cancer cells|journal=Cell Death & Disease|language=En|volume=8|issue=3|pages=e2689|doi=10.1038/cddis.2017.92|doi-access=free|pmid=28333150|pmc=5386582|issn=2041-4889}}</ref>

Daniel's research has been cited more than 4,000 times and she has an [[h-index]] of 26.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.ca/citations?user=E-6bRBwAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Juliet Daniel - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.ca|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref> She has been recognized for her research and mentorship by multiple awards, including 100 Accomplished Black Canadian (ABC) Women, a BBPA Harry Jerome Innovation and Technology Award, YWCA Hamilton – Woman of Distinction Award and a Gold Crown of Merit for Cancer Research, Barbados National Honor. Daniel was most recently recognized with a WXN Canada's Most Powerful Women: Top 100 Award.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.100abcwomen.ca/dr-juliet-daniel-hamilton-ontario/|title=Dr. Juliet Daniel (Hamilton, Ontario) &#124; 100ABCWomen}}</ref><ref>https://dailynews.mcmaster.ca/articles/mcmaster-shines-at-ywca-women-of-distinction-awards-gala/ http://www.uwitorontogala.org/honorees/dr-juliet-daniel</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://wxnetwork.com/page/2020Top100Winners | title=Top 100 Award Winners 2020 - WXN }}</ref>

She has received funding from both national and international agencies, including CIHR, NSERC and the US CDMRP (Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs) Breast Cancer IDEA Awards.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":6" />

Daniel mentored African Caribbean students at McMaster University, and within the community of [[Hamilton, Ontario|Hamilton]].<ref name=":1" /> In 2006, Daniel co-founded the Canadian Multicultural LEAD Organization for Mentoring & Training.<ref name=":6" />

== Personal life ==
Daniel was diagnosed with [[breast cancer]].<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":1" /> Following treatment, she died on April 28, 2026, in Dundas, Ontario.<ref name="globe">{{cite web|title=Researcher Juliet Daniel studied type of breast cancer disproportionately affecting Black women|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-juliet-daniel/|last=Forster|first=Victoria|date=May 16, 2026|publisher=The Globe and Mail|access-date=May 16, 2026}}</ref><ref name=":1" />
